parsed.explanation: Combined regime is protective-state care/insurance and shield laws under a restrictive federal passport, facilities and custody layer. Federal document discrepancy can trigger refusal and fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration, government-funded facilities are barred by birth sex, and federal/state custody abuse and birth-sex disciplinary placement are documented. Active litigation and state protections mitigate everyday life but do not cancel the federal border-to-custody chain, including for minors seeking care or schooling.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal X-marker processing stopped Feb 2025, existing X valid to expiry, new passports only M/F per documents; SCOTUS allowed restriction Nov 2025. Cable: document discrepancy/doubt on sex requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility, not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. ACLU suit and other court challenges are ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists. Foreign governments issued travel advisories after detentions over visa/document issues.
entry_documents.interaction: A home-passport discrepancy at entry can become a visa refusal, investigation and fraud allegation, then detention, regardless of protective state law.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution; trans prisoners report denied care and reporting stopped. Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. State prison in July 2024 transferred a trans woman to men's prison as punishment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prisons legally required since Oct 2023, under court order, to provide gender-affirming care and surgery where indicated. Federal remedies are contested and several orders enjoined, but no documented working remedy for passport or custody practices is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry/custody interaction is the severe chain: discrepancy, detention, birth-sex placement or conversion-therapy practices, with harm documented rather than hypothetical.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Jan 2025 executive order barred trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Nationally, 9+1 jurisdictions ban all government buildings, 9 cover schools plus some government buildings, 3 schools-only; 4 make certain use a trespass offence. This state's specific facility law is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 jurisdictions and capital district have no mapped ban, but map warns other sex-definition laws may affect access. This state is ranked among most protective, but that does not remove federal facilities ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection does not cancel federal facilities on federal property or federally funded settings encountered during travel.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders label minor gender-affirming care as mutilation, freeze funding, propose barring public insurance under 18; 27 states ban child care nationally. Several orders blocked or enjoined, status depends on travel date.
care_services.protection: This state has comprehensive insurance covering facial-hair removal and expanded gender-affirming procedures, among only four states, plus shield laws/executive orders enforceable against outside action and listed on national tracker.
care_services.interaction: Shield and insurance protections operate for care provided in-state, but federal funding, investigation and insurance rules may still interact; enforcement record for shield is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy May 2026 prioritizes violent groups described as radically pro-transgender; Dec 2025 reward memo uses radical gender ideology in extremist context but not as reward criterion. Federal orders direct investigation/prosecution over school gender-ideology and pronoun/name facilitation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement. National hate-crime law covers gender identity; employment discrimination prohibited under 2020 Supreme Court ruling. Only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises outing and police-interaction risk and interacts with school, facility and document enforcement, even though reward criterion and mere disagreement are excluded.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces federal sports-entry ban for trans athletes, school investigation/prosecution directives for social transition including names/pronouns, DOJ hospital subpoenas, and proposed insurance bar. A guardian/provider may face investigation or funding consequences even if visitor is not defendant.
minors_guardians.protection: Protective state shield laws and expanded insurance, plus refuge protections noted for people fleeing hostile regimes, may shield care provided in-state from outside action. Content, eligibility and enforcement record not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: State shield does not cancel federal entry, facilities, school-funding or federal investigation exposure; two Nov ballot initiatives targeting trans residents are flagged but text/status not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented for this state specifically. Nationally, bathroom trespass arrest in another jurisdiction in Mar 2025 involved handcuffing, 24 hours in men's ward, charge up to 60 days. No visitor-specific street-violence pattern for this state is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity. State is ranked most protective, but state bias-crime coverage, police response and prosecution record for trans visitors are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of documented street violence for this state is not treated as safety; police response would interact with facility and document encounters.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restriction survived Supreme Court review; facilities and custody exposures lack documented effective remedy. Ballot initiatives, shield-law type/date/enforcement, post-2024 prison housing practice, and applicability of other sex-definition laws are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several federal orders, ACLU and other challenges are unresolved, state court order mandates prison care, and ombuds/legal-aid resources exist. Remedies are partial and time-varying.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty itself is exposure: protection depends on which federal measures are in force at travel and whether Nov initiatives change state posture.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar birth-sex custody harm is documented, including disciplinary transfer to men's prison and federal conversion-therapy model. This case is safer than 0.25-C because no routine raids, extortion or frequent visitor detention in this protective state are documented and courts have enjoined some orders.

Similar universal federal exclusion on documents and facilities with weak remedy for passport refusals. This case adds documented custody sexual abuse and fraud ineligibility consideration, but state shield/care protections and active litigation offset part of that, placing it near/slightly above 0.35.

Lower than 0.55-B: secondary screening here is not only delay or discretionary refusal, it can trigger fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration, categorical federal facility exclusion, and documented severe custody abuse, whereas 0.55-B remains mainly administrative.

Much lower than 0.75-C: that anchor accepts passports matching presentation with training and tribunal compensation. Here X processing stopped, discrepancy triggers refusal, and federal facilities are barred despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a most-protective state for insurance, care and shield protection with federal rules that control entry, national facilities and federal custody. A visitor can receive protected in-state care yet still face document refusal, fraud consideration, birth-sex facilities and, if detained, birth-sex or conversion-therapy custody with documented abuse. Minors face added federal school, sports and care exposure partly shielded in-state. Courts mitigate some measures but the passport restriction stands, so final interaction remains high-risk elevated, not reduced-risk.
